title: 2022 Barker Legal Studies Trial
notes: The answer sheet in the PDF is unmarked; all answers are reasoned estimates. No shared stimuli or question figures occur in Section I.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an individual right?

options.B: Suffrage
options.C: Self-determination
options.D: Clean environment

questions.answerNote: Suffrage is an individual civil and political right.

questions.stem: A person is charged with being drunk in a public place. What type of offence is this?

options.B: Conspiracy
options.C: Preliminary
options.D: Public order

questions.answerNote: Public drunkenness is a public order offence.

questions.stem: What is the role of a Public Defender?

options.A: To represent the state in criminal cases
options.B: To give general legal advice to the public
options.C: To represent a person who has a grant of legal aid
options.D: To advise the jury on legal matters arising during a trial

questions.answerNote: A Public Defender represents legally aided accused people.

questions.stem: Which body is responsible for creating statutory guidelines?

options.B: Coroner’s Court
options.C: Court of Appeal
options.D: Office of the Premier

questions.answerNote: Statutory guidelines are created through legislation passed by Parliament.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an intergovernmental organisation?

options.B: United Nations
options.C: Amnesty International
options.D: Human Rights Commission

questions.answerNote: The UN is composed of member states.

questions.stem: A non-citizen is released from a lengthy prison sentence. Which of the following is a possibility for this offender?

options.B: Extradition
options.C: Deportation
options.D: Registration

questions.answerNote: A non-citizen may be deported after serving a sentence.

questions.stem: How can the NSW Drug Court best be described?

options.B: As a court of first instance
options.C: As a form of restorative justice
options.D: As a court of last resort for an accused with a drug addiction

questions.answerNote: Changed from B. The NSW Drug Court takes referrals from the Local and District Courts and is a court-based diversionary program (Drug Court Act 1998), so it is not really a court of first instance. B is the second option (https://www.ruleoflaw.org.au/crime/criminal-trial-processes/criminal-law-processes-court-jurisdiction/drug-court/).

questions.stem: The Australian Government decides to pass an Act which sets out a Charter of Rights. Which of the following statements is true?

options.A: The Government must first hold a referendum.
options.B: The Charter of Rights must be in the Constitution.
options.C: The approval of the Governor-General is required first.
options.D: This would fulfil Australia’s responsibilities under international law.

questions.answerNote: A statutory Charter needs no referendum, constitutional entrenchment or prior Governor-General approval, so D is the only option left; It is still a loose statement.

questions.stem: The Prime Minister predicts that the High Court will find that a Member of Parliament is not a citizen of two countries. Which concept does this prediction go against?

options.B: The division of powers
options.C: The separation of powers
options.D: The Ministerial Code of Conduct

questions.answerNote: The executive should not seek to dictate a judicial decision.

questions.stem: How is a penalty unit used?

options.A: To calculate a fine for an offender
options.B: To charge a suspect after being arrested
options.C: To calculate an accused’s bail conditions
options.D: To decide an offender’s parole conditions

questions.answerNote: Penalty units standardise the calculation of fines.

questions.stem: Which of the following supports a person’s rehabilitation into society after a custodial sentence has been served?

options.B: Control Orders
options.C: Diversionary programs
options.D: Parole

questions.answerNote: Parole supports supervised reintegration after custody.

questions.stem: A major power which the police have when enforcing criminal law is?

options.A: To use reasonable force when attempting to arrest a suspect
options.B: To arrest a suspect but only if the police have an arrest warrant
options.C: To use as much force as necessary when attempting to arrest a suspect
options.D: To arrest a suspect on the grounds that they have been charged with the same offence previously

questions.answerNote: Police may use reasonable force when lawfully arresting a suspect.

questions.stem: A member of a joint enterprise is arrested in Sydney for smuggling weapons into the country. Where would his trial take place?

options.B: Supreme Court
options.C: International Criminal Court
options.D: International Court of Justice

questions.answerNote: The alleged offence is prosecuted in a domestic court; The Supreme Court hears serious indictable matters.

questions.stem: Which of the following is true about the International Court of Justice?

options.B: It was established to deal with war crimes.
options.C: It issues arrest warrants in cases of genocide.
options.D: It does not consider the state sovereignty of nations.

questions.answerNote: The ICJ hears contentious cases between states.

questions.stem: A person, who is told a crime is about to be committed, is

options.B: an accessory after the fact.
options.C: an accessory before the fact.
options.D: a principal in the second degree.

questions.answerNote: A person told a crime is about to happen is closest to an accessory before the fact (C).

questions.stem: A 12 year old’s case is being heard in court. Which of the following statements is true about the case?

options.A: The child must establish that she knew what she did was wrong.
options.B: The Prosecution must establish that the child knew what she did was wrong.
options.C: The case can only proceed if there is written consent from the Attorney-General.
options.D: The Magistrate must prove that the child understood that what she did was wrong.

questions.answerNote: For a child aged 10–14, the prosecution must rebut doli incapax.

questions.stem: What is the role of the victim in sentencing?

options.A: To advise the judge on sentencing
options.B: To represent all witnesses at the hearing
options.C: To advise the judge about post-sentencing options
options.D: To tell the judge of the impact of the crime on them

questions.answerNote: A victim impact statement informs the court of the offence’s impact.

questions.stem: Which of the following can a trial judge NOT do?

options.A: Make decisions about points of law
options.B: Sum up both sides of the case for the jury
options.C: Instruct the jury about which facts are reliable
options.D: Make decisions about the admissibility of evidence

questions.answerNote: The jury decides factual reliability; The judge directs on law and admissibility.

questions.stem: What does the Prosecution have to establish for a charge of speeding?

options.B: Mens rea
options.C: Causation
options.D: Actus reus and mens rea

questions.answerNote: Speeding is generally strict liability; The prohibited act must be established.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT considered to be an aggravating factor in sentencing an offender?

options.A: A weapon was used in committing the offence.
options.B: The offender gained financially from the offence.
options.C: The offence was carried out in the presence of a child.
options.D: The offence was not part of a planned criminal activity.

questions.answerNote: Lack of planning is not an aggravating factor, unlike weapon use, gain or child presence.
